name: The Drowned Anchor Inn
hours: Always open to guests; the dining room serves Evening meals to anyone. Twelve rooms, mostly visiting parents, sponsors and scouts.
sight: A half-timbered inn on the quay with flower boxes, a low beamed dining room and a staircase that leans. A fire burns in the grate even in mild weather. The guest book on the hall table is as thick as a dictionary; the landlady's parrot greets every arrival with 'Mulligan! Mulligan!' It smells of woodsmoke, fish pie and furniture polish.
things: Eat the fish pie in the dining room (9 cr; the best meal in town)
Leaf through the guest book: pros, scouts, parents, a few famous signatures
Meet a visitor staying here: a sponsor's scout, a journalist, a rival school's coach
Carry bags for arriving guests on ferry days (tips)
Sit by the fire in a storm when the ferry is cancelled and everyone is stranded together
Teach the parrot a new word
Notice who takes the back stairs
secret: Where outsiders stay: scouts during the Freshman Cup and Island Open; the North Crown delegation (Days 68–69 and 164–169; Isolde's limited windows are mostly here, at the harbour and at the arena); visiting parents after the incidents (Brant's mother arrives on Day 44 (a special run of the ferry) and sits in Ward B for a week — an unnamed, devastating minor figure). Marrow's unnamed assistants and buyers lodge here from Day 61 while he takes the tower suite; the back stairs are theirs, and the crates in the stable are labelled as laboratory glass. A mainland journalist (unnamed) takes a room around Day 72 if a letter got out through the town post office; the Chancellor has her on the next ferry unless students hide her. The parrot will not say 'Mulligan' when '{H}' walks in. It says nothing at all.
